'''Robert Travis Kennedy''' is an American chemist specializing in bioanalytical chemistry including [[liquid chromatography]], [[capillary electrophoresis]], and [[microfluidics]]. He is currently the [[Hobart Hurd Willard|Hobart H. Willard]] Distinguished University Professor of Chemistry and the chair of the department of chemistry at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{cite web |url = https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/people/faculty/rtkenn.html |title = Robert Kennedy |website = UM LSA |publisher = University of Michigan |accessdate = October 29, 2019 }}</ref> He holds joint appointments with the Department of Pharmacology and Department Macromolecular Science and Engineering.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/pharmacology/robert-t-kennedy-phd |title = Robert T. Kennedy, Ph.D |website = UM Medical School |publisher = University of Michigan |accessdate = October 29, 2019 }}</ref> Kennedy is an associate editor of [[Analytical Chemistry (journal)|''Analytical Chemistry'']] and ACS Measurement Science AU.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://pubs.acs.org/page/ancham/editors.html |title = Editorial Board |website = Analytical Chemistry |publisher = American Chemical Society |accessdate = October 29, 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Editors & Editorial Board |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/amachv/editors.html}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Kennedy was born on November 11, 1962, in [[Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan]]. He earned a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry at the University of Florida in 1984 and a Ph.D. from the University of [[North Carolina-Chapel Hill]] (UNC) in 1988 while working under [[James Jorgenson]]. He was an NSF post-doctoral fellow at UNC from 1989 to 1991 with [[Mark Wightman|R. Mark Wightman]].<ref>{{cite web |title = About Dr. Kennedy |url = http://kennedygroup.lsa.umich.edu/about-dr-kennedy/ |website = Kennedy Group |accessdate = November 2, 2019 }}</ref>

== Academic career and research interests ==
Kennedy became a professor of chemistry at the University of Florida in 1991. After 11 years, he moved to the University of Michigan. He has graduated approximately 80 graduate students. Kennedy's research focuses on developing analytical instrumentation and methods that can help solve biological problems.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://kennedygroup.lsa.umich.edu/ |title = The Kennedy Group |accessdate = October 29, 2019 }}</ref> He is considered a leader in the field of analytical chemistry,<ref>{{cite web |title=The Power List 2019 |url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/powerlist/2019 |website=The Analytical Scientist |publisher=Texere Publishing Limited |accessdate=10 December 2019 |language=en |archive-date=6 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306205231/https://theanalyticalscientist.com/powerlist/2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and an expert in endocrinology, neurochemistry, and high-throughput analysis. Major contributions to analytical chemistry include affinity probe capillary electrophoresis,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=German |first1=Igor |last2=Buchanan |first2=Danielle D. |last3=Kennedy |first3=Robert T. |title=Aptamers as Ligands in Affinity Probe Capillary Electrophoresis |journal=Analytical Chemistry |date=November 1998 |volume=70 |issue=21 |pages=4540–4545 |doi=10.1021/ac980638h|pmid=9823713 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heegaard |first1=Niels H. H. |last2=Kennedy |first2=Robert T. |title=Identification, quantitation, and characterization of biomolecules by capillary electrophoretic analysis of binding interactions |journal=Electrophoresis |date=1 October 1999 |volume=20 |issue=15–16 |pages=3122–3133 |doi=10.1002/(sici)1522-2683(19991001)20:15/16<3122::aid-elps3122>3.0.co;2-m|pmid=10596820 |s2cid=39132660 }}</ref> in vivo neurochemical measurements,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Watson |first1=Christopher J. |last2=Venton |first2=B. Jill |author2-link=Jill Venton |last3=Kennedy |first3=Robert T. |title=In Vivo Measurements of Neurotransmitters by Microdialysis Sampling |journal=Analytical Chemistry |date=March 2006 |volume=78 |issue=5 |pages=1391–1399 |doi=10.1021/ac0693722|pmid=16570388 }}</ref> and ultra-high pressure liquid chromatography.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/38128291_Robert_T_Kennedy|title=Robert T Kennedy's Research Works|last=|first=|date=|website=ResearchGate|archive-url=|archive-date=}}</ref> He has been a Lilly Analytical Research Fellow, [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]], [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers|NSF Presidential Faculty Fellow]], and [[AAAS Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert T. Kennedy, Ph.D. – Chicago Chromatography Discussion Group |url=http://www.chichrom.org/meetings/meeting-archive/robert-t-kennedy-ph-d/ |website=www.chichrom.org}}</ref>
